# Section page numbering references

Original OPC/XML generated by `tools/section_page_number_fixture.py`, using our
original page-story fixture as the package skeleton. No outside document content
or renderer is redistributed. The deterministic generator creates 13 sections
covering restarts, continuation, absent/empty declarations, decimal/leading-zero,
upper/lower Roman and alphabetic formats, zero, and Roman 4000. PAGE, NUMPAGES
and SECTIONPAGES have deliberately stale saved results.

The reference application exported every fixture without saving its source:

- Main duplex fixture: 27 pages, seven completely blank parity fillers.
- Same source without even/odd headers: 20 pages, no fillers.
- Duplex with first section starting at 2: 26 pages, six fillers.
- Duplex with a distinct first page starting at 0: 26 pages, six fillers.

The offset case proves restart parity is relative to the preceding logical
number, rather than the physical PDF index. Filler pages count in NUMPAGES but
not SECTIONPAGES and have no header/footer. Roman/alphabetic zero produces an
actual space glyph (verified in the PDF text operators). Alphabetic 26/27/28
produces z/aa/bb; Roman 4000 produces mmmm. Absent or empty numbering settings
continue the value and use decimal format. The reference application reports the full
physical count for the title-zero fixture, whose package has no extended
properties part.

`reference.json` binds source and PDF hashes and stores footer/body text
for all 99 PDF pages. Browser tests check those page assignments, actual painted
strings, entirely white filler canvases and byte-identical downloads. Unit tests
also cover locked fields, unsupported-format caches, malformed declarations and
resource limits. These references establish numbering and pagination behavior,
not pixel-perfect typography for every field/font combination.
